name: MCP4725
full_name: Microchip MCP4725 12-Bit Digital-to-Analog Converter with EEPROM Memory in SOT-23-6
description: The MCP4725 is a single-channel 12-bit buffered voltage-output DAC with an I2C interface and on-chip nonvolatile EEPROM. The EEPROM stores the DAC code and configuration so the output is restored to a preset value at power-up without host intervention. It uses its own VDD supply rail as the reference, producing a rail-to-rail output from VSS to VDD. Housed in a tiny 6-pin SOT-23, it is a popular choice for generating programmable setpoints, offsets, and simple analog control voltages over I2C.

pins.name: VOUT
pins.description: Analog output voltage from the DAC, range VSS to VDD

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Supply voltage; also serves as the DAC reference

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C serial data; open-drain, needs pullup

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C serial clock input; open-drain, needs pullup

pins.name: A0
pins.description: I2C address bit selection (A0 bit); tie to VSS or VDD, or drive with logic

extra.eeprom: yes, stores DAC code and power-down config
extra.i2c_address: 0x60-0x67; A2/A1 factory-set, A0 set by pin

typical_application: Generating a programmable analog control voltage, setpoint, or offset from a microcontroller over I2C.
gotchas: Output reference IS VDD, so output accuracy and noise track the supply directly; use a clean, stable VDD
Only the A0 address bit is pin-selectable; the A2 and A1 bits are fixed at the factory per ordering code, so a single bus holds at most two of the same order-code part (A0 to VSS and to VDD)
Writing the EEPROM is a separate, slower command than writing the volatile DAC register; do not write EEPROM on every update or you will wear it out
Output is buffered rail-to-rail but cannot reach exactly VDD/VSS under load; check the output swing spec for your load
SDA and SCL are open-drain and require external pullups to VDD
